FINDING_ID: Codex_R3_F001  
SEVERITY: 0.84  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.63  
DESCRIPTION: [dynamic_management.py#L3318](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L3318) `DynamicManager.process_round()` does not reject calls made after the FSM is already terminal. It emits events, records failures, and writes convergence data via [dynamic_management.py#L3353](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L3353) before [dynamic_management.py#L3445](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L3445) finally raises from `transition()`. I verified this path: after forcing terminal state, a second `process_round()` call mutated `_round_findings` and emitted a `ROUND_COMPLETE` event, then crashed without producing a `RoundResult`.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Fail fast at the top of `process_round()` with `if self.fsm.is_terminal: raise RuntimeError(...)` before any event emission or metric mutation. If repeat calls should be tolerated, make the method explicitly idempotent and return the last terminal result instead.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: Codex_R3_F002  
SEVERITY: 0.79  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58  
DESCRIPTION: [dynamic_management.py#L1236](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1236) `RoundProgressionFSM.select_event()` can return `Event.COMPLETE` while the FSM is already terminal. That contradicts [dynamic_management.py#L1150](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1150), where `valid_events()` correctly returns `[]` in terminal state. I verified this directly: a terminal FSM reported `valid_events() == []` and `select_event(..., round_complete=True) == Event.COMPLETE`.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Add an immediate terminal-state guard in `select_event()`. Also compute `valid = self.valid_events()` once and require `Event.COMPLETE in valid` or `Event.MAX in valid` before returning either.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: Codex_R3_F003  
SEVERITY: 0.74  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.66  
DESCRIPTION: The lifecycle event protocol mislabels and duplicates round completion. [dynamic_management.py#L3320](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L3320) emits `ROUND_COMPLETE` before failure handling, convergence checks, stop checks, FSM transition, or reassignment. Then [dynamic_management.py#L3601](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L3601) emits a second `ROUND_COMPLETE` for fingerprint updates, but only on non-terminal rounds because the caller gates `update_fingerprints()` behind `if not self.fsm.is_terminal`. I verified both cases: a non-terminal round emitted two `ROUND_COMPLETE` events; a terminal round emitted only the early pre-transition one.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Emit one `ROUND_START` when work begins and one true `ROUND_COMPLETE` only after the FSM transition succeeds. Put fingerprint-update details under a separate event type or metadata field, and include `new_state` plus `termination_reason` on the final completion event.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: Codex_R3_F004  
SEVERITY: 0.68  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.71  
DESCRIPTION: Round identity can split inside a single `process_round()` call. System-level events use `self.fsm.current_round` at [dynamic_management.py#L3318](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L3318), [dynamic_management.py#L3363](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L3363), and [dynamic_management.py#L3406](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L3406), while failure events use `response.round_idx` at [dynamic_management.py#L2600](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L2600). There is no check that a `ModelResponse` belongs to the active FSM round. I verified that passing `ModelResponse(... round_idx=99 ...)` during round 0 produced one event stream with round 0 system events and a round 99 failure event. In a distributed runner, delayed or mis-tagged responses will corrupt round-scoped monitoring.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Validate `response.round_idx == self.fsm.current_round` in `process_round()` and reject mismatches, or normalize all emitted events to the manager’s authoritative round index.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: Codex_R3_F005  
SEVERITY: 0.58  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.49  
DESCRIPTION: [dynamic_management.py#L1298](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1298) `validate_no_failures()` is too weak to validate the promised “linear chain.” It only checks that visited states are unique at [dynamic_management.py#L1313](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1313). A wrong but non-repeating path like `BLIND -> SYNTH -> ROUND_2 -> TERMINAL` would still pass. This means the published reduction-property validator can miss exactly the kind of skip/jump regressions an FSM validator is supposed to catch.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Compare against the exact expected state sequence for the supplied config, not just uniqueness. Include explicit coverage for `max_rounds == 1` and for terminal transitions triggered by `CONVERGED`, `DIMINISHED`, and `FAIL_CRITICAL`.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: Codex_R3_F006  
SEVERITY: 0.55  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.57  
DESCRIPTION: [dynamic_management.py#L3119](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L3119) says `RoundResult` captures “all outputs needed for cross-area communication,” but the dataclass stores only `state: str` at [dynamic_management.py#L3135](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L3135). Every terminal outcome is therefore flattened to `"TERMINAL"`, losing whether the stop condition was `CONVERGED`, `DIMINISHED`, `MAX_ROUNDS`, or `FAILURE`. Since there is also no dedicated transition event carrying that cause, downstream consumers cannot reconstruct why the FSM stopped from stored round history alone.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Add `termination_reason: Optional[TerminationReason]` to `RoundResult`, and ideally also `previous_state` plus `transition_event`, then populate them directly from the FSM transition.  
VERIFIED: TRUE
